questions.q: What is a vendor (supplier) master record, as defined in this lesson?
options: The authoritative record of every external party an organization pays for goods or services
A record of every customer who has ever purchased from the organization
A log of every email sent to external partners
A list of employees authorized to approve purchase orders
questions.explain: Vendor master mirrors customer master in structure, but tracks parties the organization pays rather than parties that pay the organization.

questions.q: What is 'duplicate vendor fraud,' as described in this lesson?
options: Creating a second record for a real vendor with different banking details, then redirecting a payment to that account
Accidentally entering the same vendor's address twice in a report
A vendor submitting two identical invoices for the same shipment
Two different organizations having vendors with the same legal name
questions.explain: The fraud works by exploiting a lack of duplicate checking and change control: a fraudulent record with altered banking details intercepts a legitimate payment run.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what role does sanctions screening play in vendor master data work?
options: It checks a vendor's legal name against government watch lists before the record is approved for use
It is an optional marketing step unrelated to data governance
It only applies to customer master records, not vendor records
It replaces the need for a unique vendor ID
questions.explain: Sanctions screening, such as checking against the OFAC list, is a governance control layered directly onto the vendor-master creation process to confirm the organization can legally do business with that party.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe vendor onboarding as a 'gate' on the master record?
options: Because collecting and verifying vendor information before activation is what makes fraud controls like duplicate checking actually effective
Because onboarding has no connection to the fraud risks described earlier in the lesson
Because every employee should be able to create a vendor record instantly without verification
Because onboarding only applies to customers, not vendors
questions.explain: A vendor record created outside the onboarding gate — without tax ID validation, banking verification, or sanctions screening — is a known weak point that bypasses the fraud defenses.

questions.q: What is the purpose of vendor segmentation, per this lesson?
options: To classify vendors by criticality and spend so different levels of oversight and review can be applied automatically
To physically separate vendor data into different databases by country
To ensure every vendor receives identical scrutiny regardless of spend
To determine which vendors are allowed to have a tax ID on file
questions.explain: A strategic vendor supplying critical materials gets a dedicated relationship owner and performance scorecards, while a one-time vendor gets a lighter-weight record — and the segment itself should be captured in the master data.
